chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira from Mu'adh Al-Harra'i, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to call him An-Nahwi (the Grammarian), he said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I sit in the mosque, and a man comes to me. If I know that he differs from you, I inform him of the opinion of others; and if he is one whose opinion I do not know, I inform him of your opinion and the opinion of others, so he chooses for himself. And if he is one who speaks with your opinion, I inform him of your opinion.' He said: 'May Allah have mercy on you; do so.'

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque (a place of gathering and discourse)
key_terms.رَحِمَكَ اللَّهُ: May Allah have mercy on you (a phrase of approval and blessing)
key_terms.فَيَخْتَارُ لِنَفْسِهِ: so he chooses for himself (encouraging independent selection after hearing options)
key_terms.يُخَالِفُكُمْ: differs from you (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt's school of thought)

ai.seo_question: How should a scholar or knowledgeable person present differing religious opinions to people in the mosque according to Imam Al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical methodology of *taqiyya* and strategic communication (*hikma*) employed by the Imams when engaging with diverse audiences in public spaces like the mosque. Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) validates a nuanced approach where the companion tailors the presentation of opposing views to the listener's predisposition, thereby facilitating their acceptance of the Ahl al-Bayt's position without causing unnecessary friction or confusion.
